text.tspan: Up till now, we have used the simplest possible model of transcription initiation, where
mRNA starts being produced as soon as a transcription factor binds to the promoter.
A slightly more realistic model would account for the finite time it takes for this process
to activate and deactivate. We can capture this in the following model with 4 states instead of 2.
You can notice the delay in activating transcription, governed by this rate kon. This has an
interesting effect on the quality of decision making, reflected by the Fisher rate: it decreases
at high c. This means diffusion is no longer the limiting factor, and a receptor would do well
to slow down binding in order to reach maximum sensitivity at high enough c.
